bib.title: LLMs Still Can't Plan; Can LRMs? A Preliminary Evaluation of OpenAI's o1 on PlanBench

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "LLMs Still Can't Plan; Can LRMs? A Preliminary Evaluation of OpenAI's o1 on PlanBench", Karthik Valmeekam*, Kaya Stechly*, Subbarao Kambhampati (Arizona State Univ., SCAI). Preprint, arXiv:2409.13373v1 [cs.AI], 20 Sep 2024 (header "A PREPRINT - September 23, 2024"). Not peer reviewed. Research note; o1-preview/o1-mini had been out about a week.

COVERAGE: 49,660 of 49,660 chars read (all 17 pages, including references and appendices A-F). Nothing skipped. Extraction clean. Tables and Figure 1-4 are partly flattened. I did not run the figure-captions script (captions are in the extracted text).

CLAIMS (ranked)
- o1-preview nearly saturates the original small Blocksworld set, but the gain falls sharply on obfuscated versions.
  number: Blocksworld 0-shot o1-preview 587/600 (97.8%), o1-mini 340/600 (56.6%). Mystery Blocksworld 0-shot o1-preview 317/600 (52.8%), o1-mini 115/600 (19.1%), 1-shot o1-preview 247/600 (41.6%). Randomized Mystery 0-shot o1-preview 224/600 (37.3%). Fast Downward 600/600 on all.
  setup: PlanBench static test set, 600 instances of 3-5 blocks, plans of 2-16 steps. Natural-language prompts for Blocksworld and Mystery. Randomized Mystery uses random-string names with full PDDL prompts. Single run, o1 default temperature 1.0.
  quote: "Far surpassing any LLM, o1 correctly answers 97.8% of these instances. On Mystery Blocksworld, the model does not maintain this level of performance, but it does far surpass all previous models, answering 52.8% correctly."
  where: p.4 (Section 3); Table 2, p.3
- Accuracy collapses on longer problems.
  number: 23.63% on 110 instances.
  setup: Regular (non-obfuscated) Blocksworld, o1-preview, 110 larger problems, 6-20 blocks, optimal plans of 20-40 steps.
  quote: "In fact, over these 110 instances, o1-preview only manages 23.63%, and most of this accuracy comes from correctly solving problems which require fewer than 28 steps."
  where: p.4 (Fig. 3, p.5)
- Vanilla LLMs do well on Blocksworld but score near zero on Mystery Blocksworld, which is semantically identical.
  number: best Blocksworld result is LLaMA 3.1 405B at 62.6% (zero-shot 376/600). Mystery: no LLM reaches 5% (best one-shot GPT-4 26/600, 4.3%). Zero-shot Mystery is 0/600 for most models (best 5/600 = 0.8%, LLaMA 3.1 405B).
  setup: 600 instances each, zero-shot and one-shot, natural language. Models: Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3 Opus, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4, GPT-4 Turbo, LLaMA 3.1 405B, LLaMA 3 70B, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Gemini 1 Pro. Gemini 1.5 Pro could not be run on Mystery because it refused (safety filter).
  quote: "the best performance on regular Blocksworld is achieved by LLaMA 3.1 405B with 62.6% accuracy. Despite the underlying problems being identical, Mystery Blocksworld performance lags far behind–no LLM achieves even 5% on our test set"
  where: p.2; Table 1, p.2. Table columns are flattened in the extraction, so the column-to-model mapping is my inference from the column order. Check against the PDF before citing a per-model figure.
- Supplying the Mystery-to-Blocksworld translation in the prompt barely helps. The authors read this as evidence that models do not compose reasoning operations.
  number: GPT-4 reaches 10%.
  setup: Mystery Blocksworld, translation key in the prompt (Appendix C).
  quote: "However, when we provide this in the prompt (see Appendix C), performance only improves a very small amount: GPT-4 achieves 10%."
  where: p.2
- One-shot prompting is not a strict improvement over zero-shot on Blocksworld. For many models it is worse, most notably LLaMA.
  number: LLaMA 3.1 405B Blocksworld one-shot 284/600 (47.3%) vs zero-shot 376/600 (62.6%). The column mapping for this pair is my inference. The text gives no explicit figure.
  quote: "We also find that, contrary to previous claims, one-shot prompting isnot a strict improvement over zero-shot. In fact, for many models it seems to do significantly worse!"
  where: p.2
- o1 handles unsolvable instances badly.
  number: Blocksworld: 27% correctly marked unsolvable, 19% empty plan, 54% full (impossible) plan. Randomized Mystery: 16% correct, 5% empty plan, 79% full plan. False-negative rate 0% on Blocksworld and 11.5% on Randomized Mystery.
  setup: o1-preview, 100 unsolvable instances made by adding one on(x,y) conjunct to the goal of 3-5 block instances (PDDL prompts). False negatives measured on 600 solvable instances. Table 3 lists Blocksworld as 0-shot and Randomized Mystery as 1-shot. Previous models generally scored 0% on both rates.
  quote: "On Blocksworld, only 27% of all instances were correctly and explicitly identified by o1 as unsolvable." and "On Randomized Mystery Blocksworld, 11.5% of instances are incorrectly claimed to be impossible."
  where: p.5, Table 3
- o1 costs far more and takes far longer than LLMs or a classical planner, and gives no correctness guarantee.
  number: Cost per 100 instances: o1-preview $42.12, o1-mini $3.69, GPT-4o $0.65, Claude 3.5 Sonnet $0.44, GPT-4o-mini $0.02. Average time per instance (Table 2): Blocksworld o1-preview 40.43 s, o1-mini 10.84 s; Mystery zero-shot 83.37 s (o1-preview), 35.54 s (o1-mini); Mystery one-shot 82.03 s; Randomized Mystery 111.11 s; Fast Downward 0.265 s. The authors' o1 experiments cost $1897.55 within a week.
  setup: costs from Table 4. o1 bills hidden "reasoning tokens" at the output rate, and users cannot control them.
  quote: "Classical planners like Fast Downward [8] achieve 100% on our dataset in a fraction of the time, compute, and cost, while providing guarantees that their answers are correct." and "we have already run up a bill of $1897.55 for just the o1 model experiments on this benchmark!"
  where: p.3 (Table 2), p.6 (Table 4 and the text above)
- LLM-Modulo (a smaller LLM in a loop with a sound verifier) is proposed as a cheaper and safer alternative. The 82% and 70% figures are cited from earlier work and not run in this paper.
  number: 82% on a subset of the original Blocksworld test set, 70% on Logistics.
  setup: cited from [19] (Valmeekam et al. 2023, Table 4 in its Results section).
  quote: "Previous testing showed that this LLM-Modulo approach can already achieve 82% accuracy on a subset of our original Blocksworld test set, as well as 70% in the Logistics domain"
  where: p.6
- Reasoning-token use does not track problem difficulty.
  number: none
  setup: o1-preview. Fig. 2a (Mystery) shows tokens correlating with optimal plan length. Fig. 2b and Appendix Fig. 4 show tokens not rising as expected with steps or nodes expanded. Usage levels off, which the authors suspect is a cap on the preview.
  quote: "The early version of o1-preview that we have access to seems to be limited in the number of reasoning tokens it uses per problem"
  where: p.4 (Fig. 2), p.6, App. B
- o1 sometimes gives confident, nonsensical justifications for wrong answers.
  number: none
  quote: "It is almost as if o1 has gone from hallucinating to gaslighting!" Examples: a goal condition counted as true because it held at some point during execution; on(a,c) counted as true because a is somewhere above c.
  where: p.6-7
- Planning-style evidence, stated as the authors' position.
  quote: "Until now, the best way to coax sound planning capabilities out of LLMs has been to pair them with external verifiers in a generate-test framework" and "Vanilla LLMs are typically very good at translating problems between formats, and could be used to do so in concert with a classical planner" (the latter is the LLM+P idea, cited as [7, 17]).
  where: p.3-4, p.6

LIMITS
- This is a preliminary note. Only o1-preview and o1-mini were tested, and the full o1 had not been released.
- Single static 600-instance set, with no variance or seed reporting. The authors concede a static set "can only serve as an upper bound on performance."
- o1 output formatting was not reliably followed. Plans were converted to PDDL with GPT-4o-mini plus a Python parser, which adds possible error (footnote 6).
- Temperature 1.0 and OpenAI non-determinism reduce replicability (footnote 9).
- The o1 mechanism (RL-trained chain-of-thought with rollouts) is the authors' speculation. Reasoning traces are hidden.
- Reasoning-token caps in the preview may deflate cost and performance.
- Unsolvable-instance and Randomized Mystery tests use PDDL prompts, while the main Blocksworld and Mystery tests use natural language, so the numbers are not strictly like-for-like.
- The Table 3 shot settings differ between rows (0-shot vs 1-shot).
- Gemini 1.5 Pro has no Mystery data.
- Dated: models are from September 2024. The o1 results are likely superseded by later reasoning models, and the paper does not test them.
- A parallel study (not shown) is said to find that o1 does poorly on TravelPlanner and Natural Plan.

BUILDS ON: PlanBench (Valmeekam et al., NeurIPS 36, 2024; arXiv 2022). Stechly, Valmeekam and Kambhampati 2024, "Chain of thoughtlessness". Kambhampati et al. 2024, LLM-Modulo ("LLMs can't plan, but can help planning in LLM-Modulo frameworks"). Valmeekam et al. 2023, "On the planning abilities of LLMs". Helmert 2006 (Fast Downward). Liu et al. 2023 (LLM+P). Olmo et al. 2021 (GPT3-to-plan). Kambhampati 2024 (Annals NYAS, "Can LLMs reason and plan?"). Katz et al. 2024 (Thought of Search). Kapoor et al. 2024 (AI agents that matter). Romera-Paredes et al. 2024 (FunSearch). Trinh et al. 2024 (AlphaGeometry).

CODE: none worth keeping. The appendices hold prompts (Appendix D to F). Appendix C is the Mystery-to-Blocksworld key, which maps Attack to pick up, Feast to unstack, Succumb to put down, Overcome to stack, Province to clear, Planet to on the table, Harmony to hand empty, Pain to holding, and Craves to on top of.

FIGURES
- Fig 1, p.3: Mystery Blocksworld by plan length. Fast Downward solves everything instantly, LLMs struggle, and o1 degrades with length. This is the quickest summary of the paper.
- Fig 2, p.4: (a) o1-preview reasoning tokens vs optimal plan length on Mystery. (b) tokens do not rise as expected with steps.
- Fig 3, p.5: o1-preview accuracy on the 110 larger Blocksworld problems of 20 or more steps, 23.63% overall.
- Fig 4 (Appendix B): reasoning tokens vs nodes expanded.

PROBLEMS: Tables 1 and 2 are flattened and column-to-model mapping in Table 1 is inferred from order. Figure content is not in the extracted text, only the captions. No embedded instructions found in the PDF text.
